scope: Rice evidence-informed plan: broader source-specific findings and executable gaps; preserves existing page presentation

themes.title: Global arsenic patterns and speciation
themes.candidate_synthesis: Compare the direct species results in Carey’s 1,180 polished-rice samples (median iAs 66 µg/kg; median DMA 21 µg/kg) with the Iberian survey (polished-grain median iAs 0.071 mg/kg; reported brown-grain median 0.157 mg/kg). Williams reports historical total-As differences between California and South Central samples, but its iAs exposure values use an assumed fraction. Zavala adds direct species analysis in deliberately selected high-total-As samples. These findings require separate species, selection and origin strata; they cannot supply one current origin ranking.
themes.unresolved_work: Reconcile sampling dates, origin versus purchase market, polished versus brown grain, speciation subsets, reporting bounds and overlapping samples. Resolve the internally inconsistent Meharg table before using its exact country values.
themes.evidence_status: Source-specific planning synthesis of stored records; prior primary checks retain their exact scope; no new primary verification, question-level eligibility or certainty approval

themes.title: Cadmium across markets and sampling frames
themes.candidate_synthesis: Shi’s compilation reports a Cd median of 19.0 µg/kg in 2,270 polished-rice samples, including 1,167 reused observations. Compare this with Henan monitoring (6,632 rice samples; Cd detection 27.69%) and the mining-county study (220 rice samples; reported Cd mean 0.48 mg/kg). These are materially different sampling frames. Huang’s pooled estimates and high heterogeneity provide context and primary-study leads, with its combined-hazard interpretation held for correction. Censored medians require explicit substitution rules. Song adds 19,786 rice observations (mean Cd 0.062 ± 0.128 mg/kg fresh weight; 19% below LOD) and consumption-model estimates, using 2011–2015 occurrence with 2002 consumption data. The larger all-food denominator must not become rice N.
themes.unresolved_work: Build source-specific rows and review representativeness; trace the global compilation to its reused studies and preserve the distinction between source-reported statistics and a new pooled estimate.
themes.evidence_status: Source-specific planning synthesis of stored records; prior primary checks retain their exact scope; no new primary verification, question-level eligibility or certainty approval

themes.title: Lead, nickel, aluminium, chromium and uranium
themes.candidate_synthesis: The Myanmar survey reports Ni and total Cr as well as tAs, Cd and Pb; its iAs risk input is assumed at 30% of tAs. The Thai variety survey reports mean Ni values from 0.12 to 1.26 mg/kg and uses a 70% total-to-inorganic-As assumption. Ethiopian composites report Cd/Pb/Cr/Ni below quantification without verified exact limits. Add the small natural-sample Cr(VI) methods results separately from total-Cr surveys; Gama’s uranium and As compliance claims remain on hold.
themes.unresolved_work: Verify grain-level results, analytical limits, small samples and method scope. Total chromium cannot answer Cr(VI); non-detects without verified limits cannot establish an absence of contamination.
themes.evidence_status: Source-specific planning synthesis of stored records; prior primary checks retain their exact scope; no new primary verification, question-level eligibility or certainty approval

themes.title: Methylmercury and total mercury
themes.candidate_synthesis: Brombach’s 87 commercial products report MeHg 0.11–6.45 µg/kg and tHg 0.53–11.1 µg/kg; subgroup and dispersion inconsistencies require resolution. Palmieri contributes measured total Hg, not direct MeHg despite its exposure framing. Cui contributes spatially modelled grain Hg, not a retail sample distribution. Seyfferth contributes direct grain-species responses to water management. Explain why these endpoints differ rather than extending a total-Hg-only table with interchangeable mercury values. A 27-unit greenhouse cultivar/soil-Hg experiment reports differing grain-tHg responses, including no statistically detected soil-Hg effect for cultivar FA2000. Aerobic spiked pots cannot establish flooded-field MeHg performance.
themes.unresolved_work: Separate direct species measurements, total-only results and model outputs; retrieve Brombach supporting values, resolve its subgroup and dispersion discrepancies, and preserve the different material fractions.
themes.evidence_status: Source-specific planning synthesis of stored records; prior primary checks retain their exact scope; no new primary verification, question-level eligibility or certainty approval

themes.title: Grain fractions, polishing and material identity
themes.candidate_synthesis: Tran’s stored brown/white grain means differ for total As (0.16 versus 0.11 mg/kg dry weight) while Cd means are both 0.21 mg/kg. This directly challenges a universal all-metal benefit from polishing. Rahman’s fraction measurements and Limmer’s spatial imaging can explain tissue distribution, while Lockwood’s inconsistent statements about Cd localization need primary adjudication. TatahMentan adds form-specific retail tAs/Pb/Cd and essential elements; between-group brown/white differences are not paired milling effects.
themes.unresolved_work: Verify measured fractions and species; add yield and mass balance before describing polishing as removal. Imaging intensity and tissue localization cannot automatically replace a bulk-food concentration.
themes.evidence_status: Source-specific planning synthesis of stored records; prior primary checks retain their exact scope; no new primary verification, question-level eligibility or certainty approval

themes.title: Flour, syrup, protein and rice beverages
themes.candidate_synthesis: Hosojima’s composition table reports Cd 0.14 ± 0.17 mg/kg across five rice-endosperm-protein powder batches; this is product composition, not proof of clinical safety or a grain-to-protein concentration factor. D’Amato reports beverage iAs 7–24 µg/kg in 25 Italian-market drinks collected in 2022–2023. Jackson distinguishes toddler formulas containing brown-rice syrup from infant formulas without it. Meyer supplies hydrolysed-rice-formula measurements, and Zhao supplies a flour-processing experiment. Keep these direct material results separate from modelled derivative values.
themes.unresolved_work: Route each derivative to its existing destination and summarize only its implications on Rice. Verify ingredients, preparation, concentration versus dilution, and the measured material in clinical-study composition tables.
themes.evidence_status: Source-specific planning synthesis of stored records; prior primary checks retain their exact scope; no new primary verification, question-level eligibility or certainty approval

themes.title: Rice foods across product categories and markets
themes.candidate_synthesis: Gu reports fresh-weight mean iAs 155 ± 5 µg/kg in three rice pastas and 94 ± 12 µg/kg in 21 rice crackers, but did not analyze cereal iAs. Noh and Signes-Pastor add category-specific species observations; Guo measured total/unspecified As and Hg. Barber’s availability-based 566-product survey offers ingredient associations rather than attributable rice concentrations. Rajkowska-Myśliwiec’s 120 products provide measured tAs; its iAs scenarios use assumed fractions. Product denominators, basis and species must travel with every comparison. Silva adds a 36-sample co-contaminant pilot with no detected mycotoxin–reported-arsenic correlation; its claimed iAs identity and implied dry basis remain held until the primary separation method is verified.
themes.unresolved_work: Keep finished-product observations separate from ingredient estimates; verify whether each analyte was actually measured and retain formulation and market differences. Ingredient correlations alone cannot assign contamination to rice.
themes.evidence_status: Source-specific planning synthesis of stored records; prior primary checks retain their exact scope; no new primary verification, question-level eligibility or certainty approval

themes.title: Soil chemistry and redox pathways
themes.candidate_synthesis: The two-year Limmer experiment compares six irrigation regimes in 18 mesocosms with three replicates per regime. Hossain’s Cd-spiked pot experiment reports cultivar-specific grain responses across pH 4, 7 and 9; those extreme treatments do not establish a farm operating target. Begum reports grain iAs 0.025–0.08 mg/kg and DMA 0.08–0.16 mg/kg alongside changing porewater chemistry. Wei’s paired soil–rice observations add geological context, with soil-classification thresholds kept distinct from grain measurements and food law.
themes.unresolved_work: Extract the measured edible endpoint and the mediating evidence. Avoid attributing a purchased lot to a pathway from a market concentration alone, and do not generalize soil screening thresholds into food limits.
themes.evidence_status: Source-specific planning synthesis of stored records; prior primary checks retain their exact scope; no new primary verification, question-level eligibility or certainty approval

themes.title: Microbial methylation and plant mechanisms
themes.candidate_synthesis: Dai reports brown-grain iAs 78–109 µg/kg dry weight and methylated species 6.5–42 µg/kg across chronosequence sites, plus a literature synthesis of thiolated arsenic. Zhou combines MeHg-spiked soil degradation experiments with modelled grain consequences. Cheng contrasts cultivar-associated root microbial communities and harvested-grain Cd, while Mishra uses seven-day seedling exposures and tissue thiol chemistry. Integrate measured grain, soil incubation, microbial association and proposed pathway evidence without converting them into demonstrated dietary benefit. Zandi’s Cr(III)-exposed seedlings add root-plaque localization and dissolution evidence; hotspot spectra are neither edible-grain concentrations nor bulk grain-species fractions.
themes.unresolved_work: Distinguish experimentally perturbed mechanisms from associations and model predictions. Separate soil microbiome endpoints, seedling tissues and harvested grain; do not infer a demonstrated human-health benefit from a mechanistic result.
themes.evidence_status: Source-specific planning synthesis of stored records; prior primary checks retain their exact scope; no new primary verification, question-level eligibility or certainty approval

themes.title: Cultivar selection and transporter biology
themes.candidate_synthesis: Liu’s 208-cultivar source reports brown-rice Cd from non-detect to 1.61 mg/kg and direct As species, while the separate GWAS source examines 191 accessions under contrasting water conditions. Tran adds brown/white grain and QTL comparisons; Inoue’s transporter experiments help explain uptake but include non-field systems. Fu adds contaminated-field Hg–Cd cultivar and conditioner comparisons. Publication versions, genotype-by-environment stability, yield, essential elements and co-contaminants must determine transfer, not cultivar or QTL counts.
themes.unresolved_work: Trace the Liu preprint to any later version; separate field cultivar performance from association signals, yeast assays and hydroponic experiments. Verify yield, essential mineral uptake, stability across soils and the other contaminants.
themes.evidence_status: Source-specific planning synthesis of stored records; prior primary checks retain their exact scope; no new primary verification, question-level eligibility or certainty approval

themes.title: Amendments, biochar, silicon and selenium
themes.candidate_synthesis: Compare Sun’s three-year field biochar experiment with Liang’s six-treatment, four-replicate pot study; Liang’s 81.4% change is available soil Cd and must not become a grain effect. Jiang supplies multiyear brown-grain Cd with and without Se under two soil-Cd settings. Zhao reports cultivar-dependent grain-Cd responses to foliar Si. Gupta reports about 20% higher yield without a statistically detected grain iAs, DMA or Cd response. Huang and Tan extend amendment mechanisms but require exact tissue/edible-endpoint extraction. Prior selected-source review records Sun’s maximum reported field grain-Cd reduction of 26.25% and 0.12 mg/kg, with residual grain not meeting its cited criterion. Liang’s stored brown-grain reductions reach 86.2% versus untreated pots, whereas Jiang’s multiyear foliar-Se study reports 40.36% Cd reduction and 7.58% yield gain. Compare absolute residuals, units, setting and durability; a bigger percentage is not evidence of better field performance.
themes.unresolved_work: Extract exact amendment composition, dose, soil, comparator, seasons, edible endpoints, uncertainty and unwanted effects. Keep pot and field studies separate; do not promote a root/shoot reduction to grain effectiveness.
themes.evidence_status: Source-specific planning synthesis of stored records; prior primary checks retain their exact scope; no new primary verification, question-level eligibility or certainty approval

themes.title: Water management as a multi-outcome decision
themes.candidate_synthesis: Compare Limmer’s As–Cd trade-off with Seyfferth’s linked As/Hg species, Cd, methane, yield and micronutrients. The stored Seyfferth summary reports Cd increases of 50–97% and yield reductions of 25–40% in the driest conditions; retrieve the paired absolute grain values and confirm the percentage denominators before comparing with Limmer. Muehe adds a particular warming/CO₂ experiment. Resolve shared Delaware study families and keep year, regime, cultivar and independent unit intact.
themes.unresolved_work: Resolve study families, experimental units and site/cultivar differences, including the Delaware reports. Retain all tested regimes and seasons; explain how baseline concentrations affect relative percentages.
themes.evidence_status: Source-specific planning synthesis of stored records; prior primary checks retain their exact scope; no new primary verification, question-level eligibility or certainty approval

themes.title: Cooking, soaking, water quality and drainage
themes.candidate_synthesis: Carey’s 12:1 cooking-volume experiment reports 57 ± 5% lower residual-grain iAs, with unresolved dispersion meaning; this is distinct from its percolation experiments. Pogoson’s sequential chemical soaks and cooking report reductions of 79% Cd, 81% iAs and 66% DMA. FDA summarizes excess-water cooking research with iAs reduction and losses of added nutrients. TatahMentan’s washed/unwashed Pb/Cd contrasts require confirmation of pairing. Rittirong and Beene add utensil/water and mass-balance questions. Do not rank these unlike processes by isolated percentages. Ammar adds Al migration in rice–beef meals under four-pot acidification/heating/holding conditions; prolonged experimental conditions and mixed food prevent intrinsic-rice or ordinary-cooking attribution. Carey’s percolator arm also reports potassium/phosphorus losses; Pogoson’s stored starting tAs versus iAs-plus-DMA totals need arm/basis reconciliation before exact concentration reuse.
themes.unresolved_work: Reconcile the chemical-treatment sequence, analytical basis, nutrient losses, water use, waste destination and implementation evidence. Keep laboratory protocols distinct from consumer guidance and infant-food preparation. Reconcile Pogoson’s initial tAs maximum of 0.095 mg/kg with stored mean iAs plus DMA of 0.113 mg/kg; retain possible arm/material/basis differences as unresolved.
themes.evidence_status: Source-specific planning synthesis of stored records; prior primary checks retain their exact scope; no new primary verification, question-level eligibility or certainty approval

themes.title: Formulation and alternative-grain comparisons
themes.candidate_synthesis: Carey’s market comparison reports pure-rice versus multigrain infant-porridge iAs medians of 66 versus 10 µg/kg and cake medians of 60 versus 8 µg/kg, with small unequal groups. Signes-Pastor and Gu provide independent product-category context. HBBF’s rice/alternative-grain sample frame and analyte-specific findings merit review, but its conflicting Cd statements and summed-metal comparisons require correction. Ingredient correlations and cross-sectional product comparisons support formulation hypotheses, not guaranteed recipe effects or a health-weighted metal score.
themes.unresolved_work: Disaggregate elements rather than use a summed-metal score; trace mixed surveys to their original samples; assess nutrition, suitability and other contaminants in alternatives. No brand-by-brand reproduction or nonconforming-lot dilution claim. Reconcile HBBF’s opposing Cd-direction statements and prohibit an unweighted summed-metal mass from acting as a health score.
themes.evidence_status: Source-specific planning synthesis of stored records; prior primary checks retain their exact scope; no new primary verification, question-level eligibility or certainty approval

themes.title: Bioaccessibility, absorption and concentration
themes.candidate_synthesis: Bolan reports rice-grain in-vitro As bioaccessibility of 23.16–32.34% in its selected materials. Zhang’s Cd digestion experiment reports 52.07% gastric versus 18.72% intestinal control bioaccessibility; these phases are not human absorption percentages. Sadiq compares three commercial cereals using two digestion methods, with six analytical replicates per material, and Depaiva adds Al in cereal foods. Li’s transfer work links plant fractions and Cd. Explain method, material and phase differences before relating these findings to consumed dose. Cardini reports basmati total Cd of 9 µg/kg dry weight in a seven-matrix methods study. Low chemical-extraction recovery is not a measured bioaccessibility or human-absorption result.
themes.unresolved_work: Distinguish in-vitro solubilization, species transformations, absorption and actual exposure or health outcomes. Preserve deliberately contaminated research materials and limited product sample sets as such.
themes.evidence_status: Source-specific planning synthesis of stored records; prior primary checks retain their exact scope; no new primary verification, question-level eligibility or certainty approval

themes.title: Biomarkers and human outcomes
themes.candidate_synthesis: The paired 15-infant weaning study reports increased urinary arsenic species and diet associations involving rice, fruit and vegetables. The separate 187-pair cohort reports sum-As medians of 0.20 and 2.31 µg/L at six weeks and one year; age and diet change together. Du’s 56-infant thickener study reports no statistically significant overall urinary-As group difference (p=0.086). Rothenberg’s developmental cohort has substantial attrition and uses hair tHg as exposure proxy. Add respiratory and pregnancy interpretation, retaining adjusted estimates, nulls, confounding and cohort overlap.
themes.unresolved_work: Verify biomarkers and attribution to rice; assess confounding, selection, attrition, modeled exposure and actual outcome effects. Include null findings and uncertainty. Observational associations and screening-model hazard quotients are different evidence.
themes.evidence_status: Source-specific planning synthesis of stored records; prior primary checks retain their exact scope; no new primary verification, question-level eligibility or certainty approval

themes.title: Dietary-exposure and toxicology context
themes.candidate_synthesis: EFSA’s iAs, Cd and small-organoarsenic assessments supply distinct toxicology and exposure frameworks, including different chemical species, reference-point derivations and consumption scenarios. EPA 2025 remains pending detailed quantitative extraction in the stored record, so no finalized numeric output can be borrowed from its title. Separate authority conclusions, underlying reused primary studies, exposure models and enforceable food requirements. The organoarsenic assessment also identifies processing/species and analytical-conversion gaps requiring their own synthesis.
themes.unresolved_work: Verify current versions and primary recommendations before use, retain their underlying study overlap, and separate toxicological references from legal food limits and individual health predictions.
themes.evidence_status: Source-specific planning synthesis of stored records; prior primary checks retain their exact scope; no new primary verification, question-level eligibility or certainty approval

themes.title: Sampling, speciation and analytical fitness
themes.candidate_synthesis: Moreda-Piñeiro and Tian provide natural-sample speciation plus method comparisons, while Zhang’s AuNP sensor record provides spike recovery without rice occurrence data. Wehmeier supplies a candidate screening/reference comparison but its stored percentages and boundary claims need arithmetic reconciliation. Song adds rice-flour Cr(VI) below 0.1 µg/kg in the tested material and markedly different pre/post-extraction spike recoveries. Distinguish independent products from replicate analyses, validation in solution from matrix fitness, and nondetection from possible species loss during handling. Tian’s portable Cd/Pb assay reports 0.01/0.02 mg/kg LODs and comparison with ICP-MS in 12 mixed-grain samples. Extract rice-only agreement and decision errors; correlation is not analytical equivalence, and analytical purification is not food decontamination.
themes.unresolved_work: Extract recovery, selectivity, precision, reference materials, reporting limits and sampling units. Keep spiked validation solutions out of occurrence distributions and do not equate instrument sensitivity with a validated lot-release sampling design. Check pre/post-extraction species stability and rice-only method agreement; resolve Wehmeier percentage arithmetic before comparison.

themes.title: Origin, supplier and lot decisions
themes.candidate_synthesis: Carey’s historical origin/species observations and Shi’s reused global Cd compilation inform what to investigate, while TatahMentan and Xie add retail form/composition evidence. They do not validate current supplier lots. Li’s integrated regional programme is an existing implementation lead rather than proof that commercial evidence is absent. Request temporal stability, within/between-lot variation, grain form, species and sampling uncertainty, and compare joint iAs/Cd/Hg performance. Any lot decision still requires current delivered-material measurements and a defined decision rule.
themes.unresolved_work: Identify actual market coverage and dates; assess within- and between-lot heterogeneity and commercial monitoring evidence. A collection market is not necessarily growing origin; a certificate applies to its sampled scope.

themes.title: Regulatory categories and chronology
themes.candidate_synthesis: The FDA supporting document retains infant-cereal surveillance across 2011–2013, 2014 and 2018 (means 116.7, 103.1 and 85 ppb iAs), which can inform a historical comparison after sample-frame reconciliation. The FY2018 all-below-100 statement is contradicted by the official 22–142 ppb range. EU, Codex Alimentarius, China and FSANZ instruments use different species and product categories. Check current primary provisions separately; historic source comparisons cannot establish present compliance or a rice-wide legal threshold.
themes.unresolved_work: Verify amendments and native basis; distinguish finished infant cereal from rice grain, binding limits from action levels, and original instruments from translations and secondary summaries. This planning work changes no legal or certification numbers.

themes.title: Reviews, compilations and shared study families
themes.candidate_synthesis: Shi reuses 1,167 earlier observations; Huang, Jafari and Sharafatichaleshtori reuse primary occurrence studies; authority scenarios reuse formula measurements; CR and FDA reports may share sampling releases. Sripada spans multiple Cd interventions and populations, so only question-fit rice evidence should contribute. Build a report–study–sample–analyte family graph before any independent-study count or quantitative combination. Review tables are acquisition leads and contextual syntheses, not extra replications of their included data.
themes.unresolved_work: Trace study families and inclusion windows; appraise search, selection, heterogeneity and synthesis methods. A review of interventions and an occurrence compilation need different appraisal and different units of counting.

themes.title: Nutrition, yield and changing production conditions
themes.candidate_synthesis: Gupta’s yield increase without a detected metal response, Jiang’s Se/Cd grain results and Seyfferth’s micronutrient/yield trade-offs are important alongside reductions. Muehe’s stored source reports roughly doubled grain iAs under a particular +5°C/elevated-CO₂ scenario; verify exact treatment and species before use as a future-production implication. Xie adds commercial Se-enriched grain measurements, while Su and Scott reuse occurrence/exposure inputs. Nutrition claims require nutritional evidence, and Se enrichment cannot establish low Cd or iAs.
themes.unresolved_work: Separate observed production responses from future scenarios and model projections. Assess measured nutrients and intake assumptions without inferring the net benefit from one contaminant endpoint.
themes.evidence_status: Source-specific planning synthesis of stored records; prior primary checks retain their exact scope; no new primary verification, question-level eligibility or certainty approval

themes.title: Environmental sources and source attribution
themes.candidate_synthesis: Hao’s mining-area rice and Wei’s paired karst soil–grain data represent selected environmental settings. Huda’s paired irrigation/soil/plant measurements need an explicit grain basis; Bhat’s brick-kiln gradient includes bran and straw rather than interchangeable edible grain. Li’s black-shale study adds food and human biomarkers in an unusual geological setting. Compare these designs with ordinary market sampling, preserve plausible alternative pathways, and avoid assigning source contributions from a market concentration or normal biomarker alone. Xu adds 20 paddy sites within an 81-site targeted soil/grain study; source-reported high Cd/Pb benchmark comparisons need exact grain rows and historical comparator reconciliation.
themes.unresolved_work: Review design, environmental gradients and alternative explanations; preserve selected contaminated-area sampling and measured matrices. Association between soil and grain does not prove every proposed source contribution.

themes.title: Null results and bounded measurements
themes.candidate_synthesis: Retain Ethiopian Cd/Pb/Cr/Ni non-detects with unresolved exact LOQs, FDA uranium and other bounded composite results, and Gupta’s non-significant grain-metal treatment effects. Du adds a non-significant urinary-As group comparison; Song adds a small rice-flour Cr(VI) nondetection and species-recovery limits. These findings answer different questions. Retrieve effect precision and reporting limits; neither non-significance nor nondetection establishes equivalence, universal absence or a searched evidence gap.
themes.unresolved_work: Retrieve reporting limits, power and precision; avoid turning a non-significant result into equivalence, a non-detect into zero, or an unfinished search into an evidence gap.

themes.title: Organoarsenic, heating and storage transformations
themes.candidate_synthesis: EFSA’s stored 2024 organoarsenic assessment reports direct DMA(V) means of 40.0 µg As/kg in 221 polished-grain observations and 27.8 µg As/kg in 110 brown-grain observations. Its flour/drink/porridge values partly derive from a no-loss processing model. It cites thiolated arsenic formation during puffing and transformation during storage, with analytical conversion uncertainty. Dai adds grain/soil methylation context. These species cannot inherit either an inorganic-As endpoint or a blanket organic-As safety designation.
themes.unresolved_work: Retrieve primary sections, annexes and the cited puffed-rice/transformation studies; distinguish elemental-As from compound-mass units, direct data from derived commodities, and processing change from analytical artefact. Trace Meyer formula-data reuse; evaluate market weighting, censoring and unassessed toxicology separately.
themes.evidence_status: Stored-source planning lead; primary verification and outcome appraisal pending

themes.title: Integrated field programmes and implementation
themes.candidate_synthesis: Li’s stored integrated-governance study describes 2014–2020 use of pH management, low-Cd cultivars, water management and amendments, with reported early-/late-rice Cd reductions of 57% and 78% against a 2013 baseline. This is an existing implementation lead that should be assessed alongside the single-control field evidence. Its programme size, all-samples compliance statement and component-level causal attribution remain unverified.
themes.unresolved_work: Verify publication identity and full text first, then sampled hectares versus programme reach, independent farms/lots, baseline/residual grain Cd and basis, time-varying confounding, co-contaminants, yield, costs and persistence. Do not assign the bundled programme effect to any individual component or repeat historic legal comparators.
themes.evidence_status: Stored-source planning lead; primary verification and outcome appraisal pending

themes.title: Exposure attribution, life stage and biomarker meaning
themes.candidate_synthesis: Beene combines rice, water and other exposure pathways with urinary excretion, with noncontemporaneous source/cohort measurements requiring care. Ashley-Martin adds pregnancy-specific biomarker interpretation. The Spanish child cohort adds respiratory outcomes beyond the existing developmental and hypertension evidence. Li’s black-shale study adds cross-sectional food/biomarker context rather than proof of a protective Se effect. Together they prevent urine or hair concentrations from being treated as rice-specific causal endpoints.
themes.unresolved_work: Extract measured species, dietary and water inputs, sampling times, urine dilution/physiology, repeated measures, adjusted effect estimates and uncertainty. Reconcile shared cohorts and distinguish source attribution, associations, clinical outcomes and model outputs. Correct the Beene summary’s rice/water versus total-intake fraction ambiguity before using percentages.
themes.evidence_status: Stored-source planning lead; primary verification and outcome appraisal pending
